THE WORDS OF MICHAEL — COMPLETE TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — THE COMPLETE TEXT — 4Q529

1 The words which Michael spoke to the angels of The Creator in the interpretation of the vision: In the place of the great fire I received speech. And they called to me and I stood before the throne of glory.

2 And The Creator said to me: Michael, go and tell the holy ones who have departed from the eternal dwellings that they should return to their places. For I have appointed you to be the prince over all the holy ones.

3 And I Michael descended from the presence of The Creator and I went to the holy ones and I told them all that The Creator had commanded me. And they heard and they returned to their appointed places.

4 And Michael said: Blessed is The Creator who has appointed me to this service and who has shown me His face and spoken to me from His throne. There is no other like Him in all the heavens and none who rules as He rules.

5 And Michael declared to the assembled holy ones: Know that The Creator has appointed times for everything. There is an appointed time for the judgment and an appointed time for the end of the age of wickedness. These times are fixed and cannot be moved.

6 And all the holy ones said: Amen and amen. Praise and glory to The Creator who rules from His throne forever. His kingdom endures from age to age and His counsel is established above all the heavens.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q529 is a single-fragment text whose brevity has led to its neglect in DSS scholarship. It is an Aramaic composition presenting Michael the archangel speaking to other angelic beings about a commission he received from YHWH. Michael's role as a divine messenger and prince of the holy ones is consistent with his role in Daniyel 10-12 and in other Qumran texts.

[ORIT GE'EZ] Michael appears in the Orit Ge'ez Daniyel tradition as the prince who stands guard over Yisra'el. The Words of Michael presents him in a cosmic council setting consistent with the heavenly throne scenes in Chanokh. The Afro-Asiatic tradition of the divine council — The Creator surrounded by angelic beings who receive and execute commands — is the theological framework for both texts.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Daniyel 10:13 and 10:21 identifies Michael as the prince of Yisra'el who contends against the princes of other nations. The Words of Michael presents him in a broader cosmic role as prince over all the holy ones — not just the guardian of Yisra'el but the commander of the entire angelic host. This is a more developed angelology than the Masoretic presentation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The description of fixed appointed times for judgment and the end of the age of wickedness places the Words of Michael within the Qumran eschatological framework of the raz nihyeh — the mystery of existence includes a predetermined schedule for cosmic events. This is not fatalism but theological assurance: the apparent triumph of wickedness in the present age is temporary and bounded by YHWH's predetermined plan.
